paper.title_en: Finite-time quenches across first-, second-, and infinite-order transitions in XXZ spin chains
paper.abstract_en: We investigate how equilibrium quantum phase transitions manifest themselves in small systems driven out of equilibrium by quantum quenches. We consider linear ramps of the anisotropy in spin-1/2 and spin-1 XXZ chains, which host transitions of first, second, and infinite (Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless, BKT) order. We consider system sizes available in current quantum simulators and investigate how the order of the transition, the symmetries, and the ramp duration affect the decomposition of the time-evolved state into the instantaneous eigenbasis. The order of the transition determines the dynamics: across the BKT transition, moderately slow ramps already keep the system close to its ground state, corresponding to an adiabatic evolution, whereas for the second-order Haldane-Néel transition a ramp roughly three times slower is required to reach the same regime. Across the first-order transition, since the dynamics conserves the magnetization of the initial state, we observe the formation of ferromagnetic domains, separated by a single domain wall for slow ramps and by multiple walls for faster ones. Interestingly, shortly after the transition, the state evolves as a coherent beating between domain-wall states, a behavior captured by the recently proposed quantum-state texture.
